defect: The inner tube fitted as original equipment is incompatible with the wheel rim. In consequence the front tyre may suddenly deflate without warning.
remedy: Affected machines are being recalled to have the original tube replaced with an alternative version which is compatible with the wheel rim..

defect: It is possible that part of the throttle actuator mechanism can rub against the bonnet insulation and in a worst-case situation could become jammed.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and fit modified insulation material.

defect: Under some operating conditions the air suspension cradle mounting bolt may fail.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and fit upgraded mounting bolts.

defect: The power supply of the vehicle can be disrupted without warning (the alternator warning light does not illuminate) due to a break in the wiring loom at the alternator connector.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and fit new wiring loom.

defect: Advised by manufacturer for vehicles with PEKA tow bar the description of the ball end installation in the instruction manual is unclear. In isolated cases the ball end can loosen because of a wrong installation.
remedy: A new instruction manual will be sent to owners of affected vehicles.

defect: It is possible that the bolt retaining the brake pedal may become loose. This could result in the pedal going to the floor and not returning causing a loss of braking control.
remedy: Recall vehicles to check the brake pedal and if necessary tighten the securing bolt.

defect: It has been identified that there is a possibility of premature wear of the handbrake lever ratchet leading to potential disengagement of the handbrake.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and where necessary replace the original handbrake with a quality assured unit.

defect: It has been identified that there is a risk that the rack to subframe bolts have been overtightened with the possibility of the bolts and/or rack mounting points cracking/breaking. This could lead to noise/vibration or loss of steering accuracy.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles examine the steering rack mounting bolts. Renew the mounting bolts/nuts and replace the steering rack if the mounting points are cracked or broken.

defect: It has been identified that there is a possibility that the inner edge of the alloy wheels may have been deformed when fitting the tyres. This may result in the wheel breaking.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles check the wheels for damage with a special gauge and renew where necessary.

defect: On some right hand drive 156 vehicles the brake master cylinder supply pipe connectors could develop cracks and leak hydraulic fluid with a possible reduction in braking efficiency of one of the two circuits.
remedy: Recall potentially affected vehicles and replace suspect connectors and two rubber flexible pipes on the brake master cylinder with new upgraded ones.

defect: The anti noise plastic shields fitted to the bottom of the front suspension coil springs may permit the accumulation of a high level of humidity under certain environmental conditions. When combined with the presence of salt and small stones etc. this condition may cause breakage of the spring(s) and subsequent tearing of the tyre as a result of the fractured coils contacting the tyre wall.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for the fitment of a modified ventilated spring sheath and inspection of the front coil springs.

defect: Possible loss of one braking circuit due to brake master cylinder failure
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for checking and where necessary replacement of the brake master cylinder.

defect: Possible loss of one braking circuit due to brake master cylinder failure
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for checking and where necessary replacement of the brake master cylinder.

defect: There is a possibility that the front suspension coil spring could break. Should this occur the unseated section of the spring could puncture the tyre.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for examination of the front coil springs and the installation of a protector which would prevent a broken coil spring from penetrating the tyre.

defect: Potential interference between handbrake cables and rear brake pipes could lead to wear of brake pipes and in extreme circumstances loss of brake fluid which could reduce the effectiveness of the footbrake.
remedy: Recall potentially affected vehicles for a check that adequate clearance exists and realignment of the pipes if needed.

defect: Premature wear of the handbrake ratchet pawl may lead to inadvertent release of the handbrake. Problem of material hardness discovered in Quality Control tests.
remedy: All vehicles from the period of production that may have a defective lever to be recalled and a new lever fitted.

defect: Land Rover have identified a weld integrity concern associated with the rear suspension links on Freelander models. Should the weld fracture the stability of the rear hub assembly could be impaired. This may cause the vehicle to deviate from a straight line under normal driving conditions. To protect the long term integrity of these components Land Rover are implementing recall action on all Freelander models within the affected VIN range.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and replace the rear suspension links with quality assured units.

defect: Rear emergency exit door frame may fracture.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and fit reinforcing corner brackets to the top and bottom of the rear end of the door.

defect: It has been identified that there is a possibility that the front suspension lower ball joint pinch bolt has been incorrectly tightened leading to potential collapse of the front suspension.
remedy: Recall all potentially affected vehicles to check and if required tighten the pinch bolt.

defect: There is a possibility of seepage from the rear brake pipe unions above the spare wheel. This will lead to the need for periodic topping up or illumination of the brake fluid low level warning lamp and in extreme circumstances the effectiveness of the foot brake could be impaired.
remedy: Recall potentially affected vehicles to check and if required replace the brake pipes.

defect: The possibility exists that an incorrectly specified speedometer drive gear has been fitted to some vehicle transmissions .
remedy: Potentially affected vehicles will be recalled to have the speedometer drive gear examined. Affected vehicles will have a correctly calibrated quality assured unit fitted where necessary.

defect: The pivot pin that connects the throttle pedal to the operating linkage may break due to incorrect heat treatment of the pin. This may cause a loss of throttle control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the parts concerned with quality assured units.

defect: Due to insufficient clamping pressure of fuel pipe ferrule attaching the flexible hose to the pipe end fitting it is possible that a fuel leak may occur in the engine compartment.
remedy: Recall all affected vehicles remove the suspect fuel hoses and fit quality assured replacements.

defect: The engine may stop while driving and can not be restarted. The strength of the inner part of the spill valve on the fuel injection pump is insufficient and may fail as a result of repeated injection pressure. As a result fuel can not be injected into the combustion chambers.
remedy: Recall the potentially affected vehicles examine the fuel injection pump and where appropriate replace the spill valves with quality assured units.

defect: Two conditions have been identified that may inhibit the throttle pedal from returning to its normal idle position. 1) The possibility that a loose or incorrectly located floor mat may interfere with the lower edge of the pedal assembly and 2) A potential foul condition between the engine compartment bulkhead insulation material and the throttle cable.
remedy: Recall all affected vehicles to fit revised design floor mats and securing system. A revised design quality assured throttle pedal and associated hardware is also being fitted to provide increased clearance between the lower edge of the pedal and the carpet. This recall supersedes R1998/038.

defect: On affected vehicles liquid fuel may pass through the fuel tank rollover valve (mounted in the fuel pump module) and fill the evaporative canister. This may result in driveability problems fuel odour and leakage from the canister.
remedy: To correct this condition the fuel pump module mounted rollover valve must be replaced.

defect: Possibility of starter motor harness fouling on harness support bracket which may lead to damaged wiring and a potential short circuit or breakdown of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles examine harness for damage and repair where necessary. Reposition harness clear of obstructions.

defect: The front seat belt stalk(s) may fracture as a result of inappropriate stressing.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the front seat belts.

defect: A manufacturing deficiency may result in sudden failure of the tyre body and rapid deflation which could impair the control of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall defective tyres and supply quality assured replacements.

defect: A manufacturing deficiency may result in sudden failure of the tyre body and rapid deflation which could impair the control of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall defective tyres and supply quality assured replacements.

defect: 1) In isolated cases misfiring after a cold start can cause the air grid in the air mass meter to become detached. In the worse case this could jam the throttle valve causing an increase in engine speed. Fuel pipes may chafe together and/or on fuel filter. 2) Metal brake pipe may be incorrectly positioned and chafe on rear subframe.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and:- 1) Check air mass meter and air grid and install retaining ring in air mass meter. Examine fuel pipes for chafing damage and renew or reposition and secure as appropriate. 2) Examine brake pipe for chafing damage and renew or reposition and secure brake pipe as appropriate.

defect: On certain vehicles were the owner had requested to have the passengers air bag deactivated it is possible that during the deactivation process the drivers air bag could have been deactivated instead of the passengers.
remedy: Interrogate the air bag control unit and reconnect the wiring to the drivers air bag

defect: In isolated cases the securing brackets for the rear left and right seat belt retractors may be prone to fatigue cracking. This means that the seat belts for the outer rear seats may not provide the maximum level of protection under extreme conditions.
remedy: Fit reinforcement plates at the belt retractors.

defect: The brake booster diaphragm on affected vehicles may split or rupture causing a loss of brake power assistance. This can result in increased effort being required at the brake pedal.
remedy: Recall the affected range of vehicles examine the power brake booster and replace if necessary.

defect: The brake booster diaphragm on affected vehicles may split or rupture causing a loss of brake power assistance. This can result in increased effort being required at the brake pedal.
remedy: Recall the affected range of vehicles examine the power brake booster and replace if necessary.

defect: Due to possible incorrect alignment of the splines it is possible that the steering column shaft clamp bolt may be insufficiently tightened.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and examine column shaft for correct alignment of the splines. Check that column clamp bolt has been tightened to the specified torque.

defect: Possible damage to fuel tank caused during production installation of Spider roof mechanism. A fixing screw of the roof mechanism trim cover may make contact with the fuel tank and cause possible leakage.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles for examination and replacement of fuel tank if found necessary.

defect: Rear suspension toe link to hub carrier securing bolt may become loose and cause unstable handling.
remedy: Remove and examine the subject securing bolt renew bolt where found necessary ensure that threads are clean apply approved locking compound refit and tighten bolt to the specified torque.

defect: The front shoulder belt adjustable anchors on affected vehicles may have been improperly manufactured and could have inadequate strength. An anchor with inadequate strength may allow the front shoulder belt to separate from the anchor under certain accident conditions.
remedy: To correct this condition both front shoulder belt adjustable anchors must be replaced.

defect: The front shoulder belt adjustable anchors on affected vehicles may have been improperly manufactured and could have inadequate strength. An anchor with inadequate strength may allow the front shoulder belt to separate from the anchor under certain accident conditions.
remedy: To correct this condition both front shoulder belt adjustable anchors must be replaced.

defect: The roof bars may fail when loaded to the limit of their carrying capacity. Failure could result in loss of luggage.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the original roof bars replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: As a result of improper assembly of the starter motor magnetic switch an electrical short circuit may occur if electrically conductive liquid enters this area. This could result in burning of the wiring insulation and in extreme cases an underbonnet fire.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the starter motor magnetic switch.

defect: Unexpected passenger air bag deployment due to an electrostatic discharge through the air bag igniter.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and fit ground wire to passenger air bag

defect: Unexpected passenger air bag deployment due to an electrostatic discharge through the air bag igniter.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and fit ground wire to passenger air bag

defect: Unexpected passenger air bag deployment due to an electrostatic discharge through the air bag igniter.

defect: Under certain conditions the engine wiring harness may touch the bonnet hinge. With prolonged chafing this may lead to a possible electrical short circuit and if not dealt with eventual combustion.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the engine wiring harness re-routed and secured clear of the bonnet hinge.

defect: Under certain conditions the engine wiring harness may touch the bonnet hinge. With prolonged chafing this may lead to a possible electrical short circuit and if not dealt with eventual combustion.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the engine wiring harness re-routed and secured clear of the bonnet hinge.

defect: Under certain conditions the engine wiring harness may touch the bonnet hinge. With prolonged chafing this may lead to a possible electrical short circuit and if not dealt with eventual combustion.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the engine wiring harness re-routed and secured clear of the bonnet hinge.

defect: On some Punto vehicles it has been found that the seat belt pre-tensioners may fail to activate although normal activation of the seat belt is assured.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles to shorten the safety tabs in the inertia reel.

defect: The fixing bracket portion of the Pillion Passenger Grab Handle may not have enough strength and if excessive force is applied to this area such as using the Grab Handle to lift or drag the motorcycle the Grab Handle could break or partially fail at this point. This in turn could lead to the complete failure of the Grab Handle during sudden hard braking with a pillion passenger.
remedy: Recall affected machines and fit a modified grab handle.

defect: The fixing bracket portion of the Pillion Passenger Grab Handle may not have enough strength and if excessive force is applied to this area such as using the Grab Handle to lift or drag the motorcycle the Grab Handle could break or partially fail at this point. This in turn could lead to the complete failure of the Grab Handle during sudden hard braking with a pillion passenger.
remedy: Recall affected machines and fit a modified grab handle.

defect: Heat transmitted from the turbocharger may adversely affect the rubber membrane in the brake servo unit. This could result in loss of brake vacuum assistance and increase the pedal effort and stopping distance when the brakes are applied.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the brake servo unit and the installation of a heat shield between the servo unit and the turbocharger.

defect: A steel ball used to seal an aperture in the parking brake control valve may become displaced and could result in inadvertent application of the parking brake.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to be inspected for the make of parking brake valve fitted. A securing clamp will be fitted to all the affected units to prevent displacement of the ball.

defect: On batteries fitted with non-watertight caps rainwater from the windscreen may run into the battery and result in a leakage of battery contents. This leakage may damage the adjacent fabric reinforced rubber brake servo pipe and reduce or cancel the servo assistance available when braking.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have a cover fitted to the battery and checking of the brake servo pipe for damage.

defect: Some models fitted with pneumatic suspension are equipped with rotatable connectors on the rear axle brake hose connections. These connectors may leak with an adverse effect on braking performance.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the connector type fitted and where necessary revise to  non-rotatable connectors

defect: Involuntary operation of the air bag may occur as a result of an intermittent electrical fault.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a safety fuse link in the air bag circuit.

defect: Involuntary operation of the air bag may occur as a result of an intermittent electrical fault.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a safety fuse link in the air bag circuit.

defect: The main underbonnet harness may become damaged through chafing on the scuttle panel. This could result in stalling and loss of electrical functions.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for the fitment of a protective sleeve to the main wiring harness to prevent chaffing.

defect: The wiring to the air bag control unit can chafe on the brake/clutch lever. This may lead to malfunction of the air bag unit.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the air bag wiring re-routed and fixed to the bulkhead. Any wiring found to be damaged will be replaced or repaired.

defect: A defective retaining clip may allow the throttle cable to chafe against certain rigid brake pipes. This could damage the pipes and result in a reduction in braking efficiency.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the subject retaining clip replaced with a modified version.

defect: A defective retaining clip may allow the throttle cable to chafe against certain rigid brake pipes. This could damage the pipes and result in a reduction in braking efficiency.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the subject retaining clip replaced with a modified version.

defect: An incorrect load sensitive rear brake compensator may have been fitted to some boxer vehicles.
remedy: Potentially affected vehicles are being recalled to have the compensator examined. Vehicles equipped with an incorrect unit will have this replaced with the correct type.

defect: As a result of incorrect material specification the brake servo diaphragm may fail. This would result in extra pedal effort and an increase in stopping distance.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the brake servo replaced with a quality assured unit.

defect: There have been instances of cracking between the tread and sidewall of some tyres.
remedy: Cooper-Avon are contacting all current end users of the vehicles to which theses tyres may have been fitted. Where it is established that any of the subject tyres are still on the vehicle the owner is being directed to an approved local tyre dealer for inspection of the tyres and replacement of any which fall within the affected range.

defect: On certain vehicles it is possible that the power steering high pressure hose may contact the offside front rigid brake pipe. This could result in damage to the brake pipe with a resultant reduction in braking efficiency.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for a check on the positioning of the pipes involved and adjustment of the pipe clearance where necessary.

defect: Insufficient diameter of the handbrake cable may cause the handbrake to fail prematurely.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the handbrake cable replaced with a modified larger diameter version.

defect: A steel ball used to seal an aperture in the parking brake control valve may become displaced and could result in inadvertent application of the parking brake.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to be inspected for the make of parking brake valve fitted. A securing clamp will be fitted to all the affected units to prevent displacement of the ball.

defect: A steel ball used to seal an aperture in the parking brake control valve may become displaced and could result in inadvertent application of the parking brake.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to be inspected for the make of parking brake valve fitted. A securing clamp will be fitted to all the affected units to prevent displacement of the ball.

defect: The wiring to the air bag control unit can chafe on the brake/clutch lever. This may lead to malfunction of the air bag unit.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the air bag wiring re-routed and fixed to the bulkhead. Any wiring found to be damaged will be replaced or repaired.

defect: The fuel line retaining nuts may split after tightening if the recommended torque has been exceeded. This can cause leakage of fuel with an attendant risk of fire. This campaign augments recall R1997/55 but applies only to cars built after the launch of that campaign.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the fuel lines.

defect: An incorrectly positioned water hose retaining clamp may chafe on a fuel hose. This can damage the hose and result in leakage of fuel.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the hose clamp repositioned with the clamp screw clear of the fuel hose.

defect: The roof emergency escape hatch may vibrate loose from it's retaining catches and in very windy conditions could detach from the vehicle.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for the fitment of a modified pin and screw to the roof hatch mechanism and a check on the operation of the hatch operating handle. Where necessary handles will be replaced with longer versions.

defect: The seat belt B pillar anchorage may disengage from it's index plate during a frontal impact.
remedy: Potentially affected vehicles are being recalled to have the marking on the index plate inspected. Where the marking indicates that the plate is not the correct type it will be replaced with a quality assured example.

defect: The seat belt B pillar anchorage may disengage from it's index plate during a frontal impact.
remedy: Potentially affected vehicles are being recalled to have the marking on the index plate inspected. Where the marking indicates that the plate is not the correct type it will be replaced with a quality assured example.

defect: In weather conditions which favour the build up of static electricity the air bag may deploy spontaneously if the driver enters or leaves the vehicle while carrying a high static charge. This can only happen when the car is stationery and not while it is in motion.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for the installation of an earth cable to the steering wheel to conduct any static charge to earth.

defect: After extended high speed running brake servo assistance may be lost due to petrol contamination of the servo diaphragm.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the servo brake vacuum pipe and checking of the brake servo efficiency.

defect: The air bags on the subject vehicles may inadvertently deploy during a three second period after the ignition key has been turned to the off position.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the air bag control module.

defect: The air bags on the subject vehicles may inadvertently deploy during a three second period after the ignition key has been turned to the off position.

defect: The brake booster vacuum hose check valve may stick and cause a loss of vacuum to the brake booster. This will result in greatly increased brake pedal effort and increased stopping distances.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have the brake booster vacuum hose replaced with a quality assured unit.

defect: There is a possibility of a restriction in a plastic double pipe union on the brake master cylinder. This could prevent or reduce the operation of the hydraulic braking circuit.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the plastic union examined for evidence of any restriction. If a restriction is found the plastic pipe union will be replaced with a quality assured version.

defect: There is a possibility of a restriction in a plastic double pipe union on the brake master cylinder. This could prevent or reduce the operation of the hydraulic braking circuit.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the plastic union examined for evidence of any restriction. If a restriction is found the plastic pipe union will be replaced with a quality assured version.

defect: There is a possibility that the front suspension coil spring could break. Should this occur the unseated section of the spring could puncture the tyre.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for the installation of a protector which would prevent a broken coil spring from penetrating the tyre.

defect: The main cable between the battery and the master switch can contact the edge of the body panel in the boot area. If the panel cuts through the cable insulation a short circuit may occur resulting in potential loss of electrical supply and a possible risk of fire.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled for inspection of the battery cable routing. Where insufficient clearance exists the cable will be repositioned. Additionally if the cable shows signs of wear it will be repaired or replaced as required.

defect: An incorrect load sensitive rear brake compensator may have been fitted to some 306 models.
remedy: Potentially affected vehicles are being recalled to have the compensator examined. Vehicles equipped with an incorrect unit will have this replaced with the correct type.

defect: The load sensitive compensator on the braking system may be incorrectly set.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the compensator checked and where required adjusted in accordance with the manufacturers specification.

defect: Fuel may seep from the fuel filter pipe unions.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the filter pipe unions examined and secured where required.

defect: A possibility exists of weld fractures in the main frame after impact.
remedy: Affected machines are being recalled to have the original frame replaced with a quality assured unit.

defect: A possibility exists of weld fractures in the main frame after impact.
remedy: Affected machines are being recalled to have the original frame replaced with a quality assured unit.

defect: The child seat upper base frame and inbuilt seat belt retractor assemblies may not meet the appropriate EC crash testing requirements.
remedy: Integrated child seats supplied with Galaxys from Jan 96 to Apr 1997 are being recalled for replacement of the upper base frames with modified versions. In addition belt retractors are being replaced with modified units on integrated seats supplied with Galaxys built between 1st January 1996 and October 1996. Ford are also advising all other Galaxy owners who have purchased the subject seat.

defect: In some cases a sealing plug in a connector to the braking system has permitted the ingress of air into the hydraulic fluid during the recuperation stroke.
remedy: All affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the subject connector.

defect: The rectifier may overheat and cause the wiring to melt with a consequent risk of fire.
remedy: The affected machines are being recalled for fitment of a heat sink and the installation of a fused link on the main rectifier wire.

defect: Surplus grease applied to the stop light switch during production may carbonise and result in the stop lights not illuminating when the footbrake is applied.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for inspection and if required replacement of the stop light switch.

defect: The terminal blades of some wiring harness connectors may corrode resulting in a failure of electrical power supply.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement and modification of the relevant wiring harnesses. The replacements will incorporate moisture proof connectors.

defect: The rear axle securing bolts may shear.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to have the original bolts replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: The front seat belt height adjuster may not have been manufactured to the correct specification and could endanger the belt wearer in an accident situation.
remedy: Affected vehicles are being recalled to dealers for inspection and where required the installation of a new seat belt height adjuster.

defect: It is possible that a heavy impact on the underside of the vehicle could cause unscheduled activation of the airbag.
remedy: On affected vehicles the air bag control unit will be replaced with a modified component.

defect: It is possible that a heavy impact on the underside of the vehicle could cause unscheduled activation of the airbag.

defect: The seat belt mountings may detach from the rear bulkhead in an accident situation.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for the fitment of reinforcing plates at the belt mounting points on the rear bulkhead.

defect: The integrity and continuity of the welding on some units may not be to the manufacturers specification and could result in detachment of the fifth wheel.
remedy: Vehicles fitted with affected units are being recalled to Big D York agents to have the subject welding inspected. Where this does not meet the manufacturers specification the slider base will be replaced with a new unit.

defect: Wear in the area of the support bearings may lead to failure of the primary steering shaft and cause loss of directional control.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have the original shaft replaced with a complete assembly.

defect: The front wheel may oscillate and cause the handlebars to move rapidly from side to side when accelerating or passing over a rough road surface.
remedy: The affected motorcycles are being recalled and fitted with a new steering damper assembly.

defect: In a small number of cases the fuel supply and/or return pipes may detach from their connection at the fuel tank.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have the security of the supply and return pipes checked. Where any of the pipes is found to be insecure the securing clip and if necessary the tank sender unit will be replaced.

defect: The ball joints on the steering track rods and on the suspension rear parallelism adjustment may not be fully secure.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have the original securing bolts for the components concerned replaced with new examples.

defect: It is possible for the ignition switch harness to foul on the steering column coupling. This could lead to short circuiting and electrical malfunction.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for the harness to be repositioned.

defect: Instances of corrosion on the corrugated section of the lower steering shaft have occurred. This could lead to eventual weakening of the shaft.
remedy: All vehicles fitted with corrugated type lower steering shafts will have them replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: A percentage of the subject seats were dispatched with a label giving incorrect information on seat orientation.
remedy: Imp will:- 1) Suspend deliveries of new stock; 2) Contact retail customers & arrange for affected stock to be relabelled in-situ (independent) or returned to importer (multiple); 3) Write to people who have completed a guarantee card; 4) Advertise in se

defect: Fuel leakage may occur between the fuel tank body and the fuel pump mounting plate.
remedy: The affected machines are being recalled for the fitment of a modified seal between the tank and the fuel pump mounting plate.

defect: Binding of the throttle lever may occur due to the possibility of white corrosion.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the zinc coated bushing in the throttle lever with a nickel coated version.

defect: There may be insufficient clearance between the front brake hoses and the tyre inner wall. In the long term this could result in damage to the brake hose(s) with a risk of fluid loss.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for installation of a spacer to ensure adequate clearance between the front brake hoses and the tyre walls. Any hoses showing signs of previous contact will be changed.

defect: There is a risk of disengagement of the drivers seat catch allowing the seat to move on its runners.
remedy: The recall operation will check the security of the seat runner which will be replaced if necessary. In some cases replacement of the seat frame will be required.

remedy: The subject vehicles are being recalled to Jaguar dealers to have the installation of the retaining rings inspected. Where the installation does not conform to the manufacturers specification the rings will be replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: There is a possibility that the SRS passenger air bag aluminium facia panel may become detached during air bag deployment with a risk of injury to occupants of the vehicle.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for replacement of the SRS air bag facia panel and the adjacent matching facia air vent panels.

defect: Due to incorrect routing of the pipes connecting the brake pumps to the hydraulic accumulators there is a possibility of a foul condition between these pipes which if not corrected could result in brake failure.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for inspection of the hydraulic pipes concerned. Where pipe clearance is found to be insufficient this will be adjusted to accord with the manufacturers specification.

defect: Due to incorrect routing of the pipes connecting the brake pumps to the hydraulic accumulators there is a possibility of a foul condition between these pipes which if not corrected could result in brake failure.

defect: The wiring harness can cause the headlamp switch to overheat with consequent failure of the headlamps.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for modification to the light switch cable and replacement of the headlamp switch.

defect: The wiring harness can cause the headlamp switch to overheat with consequent failure of the headlamps.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for modification to the light switch cable and replacement of the headlamp switch.

defect: On some 406 models the steering column wiring harness may foul on the steering column and lead to electrical malfunction.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to Peugeot dealers to have the subject harness repositioned.

defect: Some instances of fracture of the leg on Vogel seats have occurred on the coaches concerned.
remedy: Owners of potentially affected coaches will be contacted by AVE Berkhof and requested to examine the seat legs. Where they are broken or show signs of impending failure replacements will be supplied by AVE Berkhof. Where legs are intact a kit to reinforce

defect: The brake servo may not release fully allowing the brake pads to remain in contact with the brake discs. This could result in possible overheating and loss of braking efficiency.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of an additional pull off spring to the brake servo.

defect: Rainwater may accumulate in the front door latch mechanism and whilst in a frozen condition may inhibit correct operation of the latches.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and protect/lubricate the front door latch mechanisms with a special water repellent grease

defect: The blanking bolts fitted to redundant seat belt mounting points may be excessively long and could chafe on the rear brake hoses. This could damage the hoses and lead to loss of brake fluid.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled for removal of the subject bolts. These are being replaced with a suitable plastic rivet.

defect: Under certain circumstances it is possible that the front right hand door may not latch properly.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have the operation of the front right hand door checked. In all cases a modified screw will be fitted to the lock to eliminate the concern but where the check indicates that the latch may be binding

defect: The valve hole in the steel road wheel is 0.5mm out of its correct position. This results in a poor valve fit and loss of tyre air pressure.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have the original wheels replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: Should the low brake fluid warning lamp bulb fail the bulb check facility is not enabled to check this condition.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled by the manufacturer for a minor wiring modification to the circuit concerned.

defect: Should the low brake fluid warning lamp bulb fail the bulb check facility is not enabled to check this condition.

defect: On some Transit Ambulance vehicles the split charge relay is insufficiently rated for its application. Additionally on these same vehicles the engine compartment wiring loom is equipped with unsatisfactory insulation.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a new level charge relay. At the same time the engine compartment wiring loom will be inspected replaced if damaged or retaped with new level insulation tape if undamaged.

defect: The rotor blades in the brake vacuum pump may have a rough surface and be subject to wear. In the worst case the blades may break causing loss of brake vacuum assistance and resulting in increased stopping distances.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to Toyota Dealers for replacement of the vacuum pump blades and rotor.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original trailing arm bolts with those of an improved material.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a bypass valve to the heat exchanger inlet and a non-return valve to the system. At the same time the heat exchanger box will be lined with absorbent foam.

defect: Due to possible defective sealing there is a risk of seepage from the fuel feed pipe where it connects to the injector rail on some 405 models.
remedy: All vehicles potentially affected by this campaign are being recalled to Peugeot dealers for the fitment of a modified clip to the fuel feed pipe.

defect: The throttle plate screws may not have been sufficiently torqued. This could result in sticking of the throttle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a replacement throttle housing.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of new seals to the brake master cylinder. At the same time the brake/clutch hydraulic systems will be purged of the original fluid and replenished. New clutch hoses will also be fitted.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of the latest version vacuum line.

remedy: Engineers from Stoves plc will check the torque of the relevant gas connection and rectify any looseness where required.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and:- 1) Replace the original seat belt buckle and its associated pretensioner control by new Autoliv components. 2) Upgrade the drivers airbag to the latest specification.

defect: On vehicles equipped with both driver and passenger air bags unscheduled illumination of the air bag warning light may occur in conditions of low ambient temperature.

defect: Under certain loading conditions or as a result of incorrect installation the roof rack may become loose and fall from the vehicle.
remedy: Owners who have purchased the subject roof racks are being contacted by Toyota dealers and requested to take the vehicles back for the fitment of improved clamps to the roof rack system.

defect: As a result of a small dimensional error the Bowden cable which actuates the braking system could detach. Should this occur the braking system would fail to operate.
remedy: The affected caravans are being recalled to have the subject cables replaced with quality assured versions.

defect: In high stress conditions the tyres fitted to the subject vehicles may lose pressure. The tyres concerned are Michelin size 225/60R 1698W CXKA.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to Audi dealers to allow the tyres to be identified and replaced where appropriate.

defect: It is possible that 6 ply rated tyres may have been fitted instead of the 8 ply rated tyres specified.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to have the tyre ply ratings checked and where necessary to have correctly rated tyres fitted.

defect: 1) Due to a defect in the clutch master cylinder the clutch may not disengage. 2) Water ingress to brake servo. 3) The front brake hoses may be incorrectly routed and could in some circumstances contact the retaining bracket nut. 4) Possible contamination
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and:- 1) Check build date and replace clutch master cylinder where required. 2) Fit a water shield to the brake servo to protect the servo push rod. 3) Check the routing of the front brake hoses re-routing where required.

defect: The wheel chair lift may collapse due to weld failure. Whilst this is likely to be restricted to a particular batch of units the manufacturer will rework all the subject lifts as a precautionary measure.
remedy: The end user will be advised by the manufacturer to take affected vehicles to Ratcliff agents for inspection and if required modification.

defect: Possibility that the tyres may progressively lose pressure in service due to breaching of thin spots in the tyre inner liner.
remedy: Recall potentially affected tyres and replace with quality assured units.

defect: The tongue at the end of the seat belt has not been hardened to the correct specification.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the seat belt assembly.

defect: The seat carrying handle may fracture.
remedy: The manufacturer is contacting owners via an advert in most popular newspapers as well as issuing a press release to relevant magazines. This will advise owners to contact the manufacturer on a dedicated hot line when on advising of the seat manufacturer

defect: The fasteners securing the alternator circuit fuse to the power distribution centre may not be correctly clamped. This could result in arcing at the connection with a possibility of an under bonnet fire.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the power distribution centre fuse with a fuse link.

defect: The fasteners securing the alternator circuit fuse to the power distribution centre may not be correctly clamped. This could result in arcing at the connection with a possibility of an under bonnet fire.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the power distribution centre fuse with a fuse link.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and remove the steering box pinion end bolts one by one to check the condition of the threads Any bolt showing signs of thread damage will be replaced and in all cases the bolts will be retightened in the correct sequence

defect: On vehicles where the rear axle mounting arrangement is by means of studs and bolts the axle assembly may become loose to the vehicle underbody.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of modified axle mounting blocks to the vehicle underbody and replacement of the subject studs and nuts by bolts.

defect: The pulley on the engine cooling fan may loosen causing the fan motor to seize leading to a possible electrical overload with fire risk.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a modified cooling fan and pulley.

defect: The bearing on the engine cooling fan may seize resulting in an electrical overload with potential fire risk.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a cooling fan which incorporates a modified bearing.

defect: The bolts securing the components of the multi piece wheel rim may loosen slightly. This can result in loss of tyre pressure.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the wheel rims with quality assured examples secured by bolts treated with locking compound.

defect: As a consequence of broken or missing spot welds leakage from the fuel tank may occur at the fuel pump mounting flange.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the fuel tanks. Where any spot welds are broken or missing the fuel tank will be replaced.

defect: A specific batch of Marangoni 165 R13 M500 tyres may experience pressure loss due to cracking at the join of the tread and sidewall.
remedy: The importer has written to all end users of the subject tyres advising them to take their vehicle back to the supplier to have the tyre inspected. Any tyres found to belong to the suspect batch will be replaced.

defect: The rear suspension composite links are below specification and may develop small stress cracks at the aluminium eye end. Failure of the link(s) would affect the security of the rear axle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the suspension links with quality assured examples.

defect: It is possible that some Mondeo vehicles may have been fitted with a right hand front brake caliper where the casting is not to specification. In time this may result in fluid leakage with the loss of one brake circuit.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for a check on the manufacturing date of the subject caliper. Caliper units falling within the affected range will be replaced.

defect: A number of the subject vehicles have been fitted with seat belts manufactured by TRW the attachment systems of which may not remain secure in an accident situation.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles check the date of production on the seat belt buckles and replace those within the critical batch.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for rerouting of the rear brake hoses. Any hose found to be damaged will be replaced.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of two new metal brake pipes which have an improved securing arrangement.

defect: The steering column may have been misaligned during assembly. This could cause fatigue in the column and result in loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the steering column. Where misalignment is found the steering column assembly will be replaced.

defect: The three bolts which secure the stub axle to the spring strut may not have been fully torqued on initial assembly.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the torque setting on the bolts involved retorqueing as required. Any bolts found to have been loose (as distinct from being insufficiently torqued) will be replaced.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the handbrake unit and lubrication of the pawl mechanism. Any damaged parts will be replaced at the inspection.

defect: The cover sleeve on the exhaust tail pipe may have been attached by two instead of four spot welds. There is therefore a possibility that the cover sleeve could detach from the tail pipe whilst driving.
remedy: The affected vehicles will be recalled to Porsche dealers for inspection. Any tail pipes where the cover sleeves are attached by two welds will be replaced with four weld version pipes.

defect: In the event of an exhaust tail pipe fracture an unacceptably high level of heat radiation may occur in the area surrounding the fuel tank.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the installation of a protective shield over the fuel tank.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a modified cooling fan and pulley.

defect: As a result of a machining discrepancy the steering box output shaft may fail resulting in loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the steering boxes with quality assured versions.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a bypass valve to the heat exchanger inlet and a non-return valve to the system. At the same time the heat exchanger box will be lined with absorbent foam.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles remove the relevant nut apply locking compound to the threads and replace and tighten the nut to the manufacturers specified torque.

defect: The method of coupling the two sections of the brake actuating rod is unsatisfactory.
remedy: The operators of all the affected trailers will be contacted and provided with a modified brake rod coupling pin.

defect: The battery main cable may chafe against the front cross member. This could result in a short circuit and possible fire risk.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of an additional cable clamp which will hold the battery cable clear of the cross member. any cables found to have a chafe condition will be replaced.

defect: During manufacture the braking systems were filled with mineral oil from identified batches which could have an adverse effect on braking performance.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to have the braking systems drained and filled with new mineral oil.

defect: The stop light switch on a small number of the subject vehicles may not operate as intended. Should this occur the stop lights may fail to illuminate when the footbrake is applied.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the stop light switch with a switch of the latest specification.

defect: The stop light switch on a small number of the subject vehicles may not operate as intended. Should this occur the stop lights may fail to illuminate when the footbrake is applied.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the stop light switch with a switch of the latest specification.

defect: It is possible that the two bolts securing the rear brake cylinder to the brake back plate may not have been fully tightened. If the bolts were to come loose the efficiency of that brake circuit could be impaired.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to tighten the subject bolts to the correct specification.

defect: There is a risk of scalding to occupants of the front seats as a result of hot coolant leaking from the heater matrix into the passenger compartment.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the heater matrix. Where this is found to be of an unmodified design (visually apparent) it will be replaced with a modified unit.

defect: The steering idler arm may not have adequate end clearance on its fulcrum and could pick up on its retaining nut shearing the split pin. This could allow detachment of the nut with an adverse effect on steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check that the steering idler arm has adequate end clearance on its fulcrum. Where the clearance is insufficient the correct clearance will be established by shimming.

defect: Under certain circumstances a front flexible brake hose may split leading to fluid loss and reduced brake performance.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of modified front brake hoses.

defect: The tyres on the affected vehicles may fail as a result of damage sustained when being fitted to the road wheels.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the subject tyres.

defect: The hydraulic hoses to the rear brake calipers may have been incorrectly routed. This could result in contact between the hose and the suspension system with consequent damage to the hose.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to check and where necessary re-route the subject hoses. Any damaged hoses will be replaced.

defect: Under conditions of heavy braking the footbrake relay cross shaft ball joint may detach from its left hand mounting. This would result in failure of the service brake.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check that the ball joint is properly located in its bush. Where this is not the case the mounting assemblies will be adjusted or replaced as necessary.

defect: Isolated instances of cracking of the front hubs have been recorded on high mileage vehicles.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the subject hubs with modified versions.

defect: The appliance mounted water tank may break loose and hit the rear of the crew cab in an accident situation.
remedy: Recall the affected appliances and reinforce the existing water tank security measures by attaching the tank to the chassis rear crossmember with high tensile duplex nylon ties.

defect: The headlamp switch may overheat and result in headlamp failure.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitting of a cable harness with control relay. In addition the light switch is to be replaced on Passat and Golf Ecomatic models as appropriate.

defect: The headlamp switch may overheat and result in headlamp failure.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitting of a cable harness with control relay. In addition the light switch is to be replaced on Passat and Golf Ecomatic models as appropriate.

defect: The seat belt fixings may be loose at the frames on both front seats. Should these fixings come adrift the effectiveness of the seat belt will be reduced in the event of an accident.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the torque of the belt fixing retaining bolts on both front seats retorqueing if required.

defect: The front seat belt lower attachment rail may be of insufficient strength and could fail in the event of an accident.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original seat belt attachment rail with a redesigned version.

defect: Interference could occur between the gearbox wiring harness and the cover for the brake pedal cross shaft located in the front foot well. In time this could damage the harness and cause a short circuit with a consequent risk of fire.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and protect the wiring harness by fitting a length of protective strip to the lower edge of the cross shaft cover.

defect: On ABS equipped Punto vehicles contact may take place between the brake compensator springs and the rear (metal) brake pipes. This could damage the pipes causing loss of brake fluid and reducing the efficiency of the service brake.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and secure the subject brake pipes to eliminate the possibility of any contact with the compensator springs. Any brake pipes found to be damaged will be replaced.

defect: On ABS equipped Punto vehicles contact may take place between the brake compensator springs and the rear (metal) brake pipes. This could damage the pipes causing loss of brake fluid and reducing the efficiency of the service brake.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and secure the subject brake pipes to eliminate the possibility of any contact with the compensator springs. Any brake pipes found to be damaged will be replaced.

defect: S maximum speed rated tyres have been fitted. As the vehicle maximum capability exceeds the maximum speed rating of the S rated tyre vehicle stability could be adversely affected on a vehicle travelling in excess of the speed rating.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the tyres with T maximum speed rated examples.

defect: The nuts securing the road wheels may not have been tightened to the correct torque and could become loose.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and tighten the wheel nuts to the correct torque. Any damage to wheels or studs caused as a result of undertorqueing will be addressed at the recall.

defect: Due to misplacement of the cap ply tyres may lose pressure through a crack in the butyl inner liner. This may have an adverse affect on vehicle control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check/replace the tyres as necessary with a different construction tyre.

defect: Some passenger seat pedestals may have been incorrectly attached to the vehicle floor. This could result in the seats detaching from the floor in an accident situation.
remedy: The affected vehicles are being recalled to have modifications to the seat pedestals carried out. The modified pedestals will be secured by bolts through the steel section of the floor.

defect: The welding on the front suspension arm locating lug may not be to the manufacturers specification.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and inspect the integrity of the subject welding. Where required the welding will be reworked to comply with the manufacturers specification.

defect: As a result of tightness in the throttle spindle and/or fouling of the speed control cable on the inlet manifold the throttle may not return to the idle position when the accelerator pedal is released.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the speed control cable with the latest level type and if necessary also replace the throttle body assembly with the latest level type.

defect: The spherical portions of certain lower suspension ball joints were produced with surfaces which were not smooth. The resulting friction could result in rapid wear and may lead to separation of the ball joint.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the subject ball joints with quality assured examples.

defect: As a result of water penetration corrosion may be present on the brake pressure warning switch connection. This could result in the loss of braking system pressure and may also negate the ABS function.

defect: There is a possibility that the thread insert which attaches the seat belt catch to the power seat slide rail may not have been manufactured to the vehicle makers standards.
remedy: Recall all potentially affected vehicles for inspection and replacement of the thread inserts as required.

defect: As built the stop lamp is not illuminated by application of the front brake.
remedy: All the affected scooters to be recalled and modified so that the stop lamp is illuminated by application of the front brake.

defect: Some vehicles with alloy wheels may have been supplied with an unsuitable space saver spare wheel. If fitted this spare wheel could cause interference with braking system components.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace any unsuitable spare wheels with correctly specified versions.

remedy: A) Volvo have written to all involved customers advising them as a short term measure not to use the jack originally supplied with the vehicle. B) The original jacks are being replaced with quality assured units as soon as these become available.

defect: The wiring loom from the ignition coil to the ECU may chafe on a cylinder head bolt. This could eventually result in an electrical short circuit and/or fire risk.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of brackets and cable ties to secure the wiring loom clear of the cylinder head bolt in question.

defect: Due to production tolerances at the halfshaft splines the rear wheel bearings may not have been correctly pre-loaded during assembly. This could lead to bearing damage and premature failure.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the halfshaft flange connection. Where this is outside prescribed tolerances the halfshaft and roller bearing will be replaced.

defect: As a result of a quality problem in the manufacture of the front brake discs the vehicle may pull to the left when the footbrake is applied.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace both front brake discs with quality assured examples.

defect: The fuel tank sending unit gasket may crack resulting in the potential for fuel leakage.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for straightening of the sending unit flange and the fitment of a new gasket.

defect: There is a possibility of a foul condition between the lower steering linkage heatshield and a high pressure hydraulic pipe that feeds the front brakes on left hand drive naturally aspirated cars.

remedy: Recall the affected caravans for the fitment of a mechanical parking brake.

defect: The security siren wiring terminal which is tied back by the left hand headlamp assembly has not been sufficiently insulated. This could result in a short circuit.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and fit a plastic insulating sleeve to the subject terminal.

defect: Minor cracking of the floor can occur around the handbrake lever mounting points. If this is ignored the effectiveness of the parking brake may be reduced.
