defect: The torque of the track rod end retaining nuts may relax and allow the nuts to loosen.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the existing track rod end nuts with quality assured examples.

defect: The front seats may not lock properly on the longitudinal adjustment/mounting rails.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of new trigger springs to the seat adjusting mechanism.

defect: The wheel nuts do not meet the manufacturer's specification. This could result in road wheel loss.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original wheel nuts with quality assured examples.

defect: It is possible that installation of the front brake hoses has not been correctly carried out during initial assembly.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of replacement brake hoses.

defect: As a result of an assembly fault the bolts securing the ball joints on the wishbone may loosen. In extreme cases this could result in loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for a check on the torque of the ball joint mounting nuts/bolts. If any bolt is insufficiently torqued all three mounting bolts will be replaced.

defect: As a result of an assembly fault the bolts securing the ball joints on the wishbone may loosen. In extreme cases this could result in loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for a check on the torque of the ball joint mounting nuts/bolts. If any bolt is insufficiently torqued all three mounting bolts will be replaced.

defect: The brake light switch may stick in the on or off position.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles check and where necessary replace the brake light switch with a quality assured unit.

defect: The service brake foot control valve may be defective. This could result in the loss of both braking circuits.
remedy: Recall the defective vehicles to check the subject valve. Defective valves will be replaced with a new unit.

defect: The service brake foot control valve may be defective. This could result in the loss of both braking circuits.
remedy: Recall the defective vehicles to check the subject valve. Defective valves will be replaced with a new unit.

defect: The front brake caliper brake adjusting mechanism may seize due to the ingress of water over a period of time.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the caliper with a version incorporating improved sealing arrangements.

defect: A possibility exists that excessive torque generated when turning on the headlamp switch may induce an internal open circuit and cause the headlamps to go out.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the headlamp switch with a revised component.

defect: The driving seat rail on manually adjustable seats may be subject to fatigue cracking.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original seat rails with quality assured examples.

defect: The steering shaft top universal clamping bolt may loosen .This will allow free movement in the steering and if not rectified could lead to loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the steering shaft top universal clamping bolt and nut with new components.

defect: The steering shaft top universal clamping bolt may loosen .This will allow free movement in the steering and if not rectified could lead to loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the steering shaft top universal clamping bolt and nut with new components.

defect: Due to the effect of corrosion on the aluminium spacer at the master cylinder mounting it is possible for the brake master cylinder to detach from the airpac unit rendering one half of the service brake system inoperative.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a re-designed spacer to the brake master cylinder mounting.

defect: A small batch of semi-trailers were supplied with an incorrect airspring support plate. This could result in a reduction in trailer roll performance.
remedy: The operators of the subject semi-trailers are being advised of the situation and supplied with correctly specified airspring support plates for retro-fitment to the trailer suspension. Operators to advise ROR when the plates have been fitted.

defect: Crack like surface defects may be present on the mould parting line on the rear axle side parts.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and inspect the rear axle side parts for surface defects where these are present the original side part(s) will be replaced with quality assured parts.

defect: A defective seal may allow fluid to leak from the caliper unit with a consequent adverse affect on braking performance.
remedy: Beason-Cooke have written to all their 45 distributors instructing them to return all the potentially affected units held in stock and to retrieve any units sold to end users.

defect: On some cars a hose longer than specified could have been erroneously fitted with consequent possible interference with the engine. Such interference could in the long run cause the perforation of the hose oil leakage and a potential risk of fire.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and a check on the length of the hose. In cases where the hose is found to be too long it will be shortened to the right length or if damaged will be replaced.

defect: The engine wiring harness may chafe on the anti-lock braking control valve bracket. As a result the wiring may short leading to failure of the ignition or fuel injection system causing the engine to stop without warning.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and install a plastic protector sleeve to the wiring harness in the area of the ABS control valve bracket. Any section of the harness found to be damaged through contact will be repaired prior to sheathing.

defect: The handbrake cable may chafe on the fuel filler pipe causing perforation of the pipe and leakage of fuel.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for repositioning and securing of the handbrake cable to ensure adequate clearance between the cable and the filler pipe. At the same time any filler pipes found to be perforated will be replaced.

defect: The front brake discs/pads could be affected by slush water or salt when driving in snow or heavy rain. This could adversely affect the efficiency of the brakes upon initial application.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the front brake disc shields with modified units giving increased weather protection.

defect: As a result of engine movement a wiring harness may chafe on a steel brake pipe adjacent to the brake master cylinder. This could cause short circuiting and possible loss of braking efficiency should the brake fluid temperature rise as a result.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a modified clip to the wiring harness. Additionally the harness will be sheathed for additional protection in the area adjacent to the brake pipe.

defect: It is possible that the exhaust downpipe may separate from the upper flange and drop onto the starter motor terminal causing damage to the vehicle wiring loom. This may result in the loss of various electrical circuits.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the exhaust downpipe with the current production component.

defect: It is possible that the exhaust downpipe may separate from the upper flange and drop onto the starter motor terminal causing damage to the vehicle wiring loom. This may result in the loss of various electrical circuits.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the exhaust downpipe with the current production component.

defect: The hub bearings in some TE 9000 axles may be liable to premature failure. If not detected this could result in hub seizure or wheel and hub detachment.
remedy: Supply sufficient replacement hubs and bearings to all operators of affected trailers and monitor the return rate of displaced units to ensure full coverage of the vehicle parc.

defect: The transmission shift cable lock pin may become ineffective. In consequence the gear lever position may not match the actual gear position selected in the transmission.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the lock pin with a modified type.

defect: The transmission shift cable lock pin may become ineffective. In consequence the gear lever position may not match the actual gear position selected in the transmission.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the lock pin with a modified type.

defect: It is possible that the front brake pipe may be contacted by the anti-roll bar link rod. In extreme conditions this may result in fluid leakage and partial loss of braking.
remedy: The affected vehicles will be recalled and inspected for contact between the brake pipes and the anti-roll bar link. If no contact has taken place the pipe(s) will be re-set to ensure adequate clearance . Any pipes showing signs of contact will be replaced

defect: Due to the possibility of incomplete application of the parking brake by the driver the vehicle could roll away when parked.
remedy: The manufacturer will write to all Xantia owners enclosing an amendment for insertion in the vehicle handbook. This will amplify and reinforce the instructions relating to the operation of the parking brake.

defect: 1) Bonnet catch securing bolts may slacken in service allowing movement of the lock mechanism. This may result in the bonnet lifting. 2) Autoliv-Klippan seat belt pre-tensioners may be faulty.
remedy: 1. Replace the bonnet catch fixing bolts with screws and lock nuts. 2. Substitute any Autoliv-Klippan pre-tensioners with TRW-REPA equipment.

defect: Suspension trailing arms may fracture forward of the axle beam. This may result in damage to the suspension or detachment of the axle.
remedy: Recalled trailers to be modified in 3 areas to reduce the stress levels and maintain tightness at the connection between the trailing arms and the axle beam viz 1)Replace axle bracket location plates with tee shaped key plates. 2) Replace square U-bolt

defect: Under extreme circumstances rear wheel lock up could occur during heavy braking. This is due to the fitment of an incorrect brake modulator valve.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original brake modulator valve with a modified example.

defect: It is possible that cracking may occur around the rear fixing holes of the stabiliser housing.
remedy: Recall the affected caravans and replace the original stabilisers with quality assured units.

defect: There is a risk of accelerator cable breakage due to cable kinking when the accelerator pedal is released suddenly.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a modified accelerator pedal.

defect: The rear heater blower resistor can become electrically overloaded due to binding or seizure of the heater blower. The overloaded resistor may become hot enough to ignite the plastic air pipe in which it is located.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the installation of a modified resistor unit which incorporates a thermal link.

defect: The aluminium couplers have been found to have cracks in the welds attaching the crossmembers to the side members. This could result in the trailer becoming uncoupled from the tractive unit
remedy: The complete upper coupler to be replaced by Fruehauf with a fully checked and modified replacement.

defect: The shock absorber top bracket may fail leading to a deterioration in handling quality
remedy: The affected trailers are being recalled for strengthening of the shock absorber top brackets.

defect: In some cases the alloy wheel retaining bolts may be of insufficient length and fail to achieve sufficient penetration into the threads in the hub.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the suspect bolts with longer versions.

defect: In some cases the alloy wheel retaining bolts may be of insufficient length and fail to achieve sufficient penetration into the threads in the hub.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the suspect bolts with longer versions.

defect: Possible leakage of fuel on the low pressure side of the system.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles examine and rectify any sources of fuel leakage and modify two connections within the system by the fitment of revised connectors.

defect: It is possible for water to enter the injection mechanism resulting in a sudden loss of engine power.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the fuel distributors injectors and hoses.

defect: The headlamp wiring harness may chafe against the shroud panel and result in possible short circuit with sudden failure of the headlamps.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and shorten the headlamp wiring harness to eliminate possible chafing on the shroud panel. In cases where the harness has been damaged by chafing the damaged section of wiring will be cut out and replaced together with t

defect: In isolated instances a floating caliper may have been installed in combination with a ventilated brake disc at the offside front wheel station. Should this be the case excess caliper movement may occur as pad wear progresses.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to check for the correct caliper/disc combination replacing any incorrect calipers with the correct version

defect: The welding attaching the front suspension lower wishbone bracket to the subframe may be suspect. In extreme conditions this could affect the driving quality of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the integrity of the subject welding. Where this is not to specification the subframe attachment will be reinforced by bolting or in extreme cases the subframe will be changed.

defect: The windscreen wiper motor and passenger side wiper arm may be of insufficient strength and could fail under extreme operating conditions with loss of wiper action.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the wiper motor and passenger side wiper arm with modified components.

defect: A. Potential loss of electrical power in any one of the fuse board circuits e.g. lights or windscreen wipers) due to poor quality soldered connections and possible damage to wiring behind the central console as a result of contact with the heater
remedy: A. Replace the fuse board with a quality assured unit and fit a protective clip to the heater controls on all the affected vehicles.

defect: The drivers footwell air outlet nozzle can become detached and may obstruct footbrake pedal movement.
remedy: Plaxtons have written to every operator of potentially affected vehicles advising details of a minor modification to the method of securing the subject nozzle. This work will be carried out by the operators who will advise Plaxtons when it is compl

defect: The drivers footwell air outlet nozzle can become detached and may obstruct footbrake pedal movement.
remedy: Plaxtons have written to every operator of potentially affected vehicles advising details of a minor modification to the method of securing the subject nozzle. This work will be carried out by the operators who will advise Plaxtons when it is compl

defect: Insufficient clearance between the ratchet internal mechanism and the handbrake lever sideplates may lead to misapplication of the parking brake resulting in the vehicle not being held.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicle for replacement of the original handbrake lever with a revised version.

defect: The security of the fuel filler hose to tube joint may be insufficient due to clip size and clamping capability. If ignored fuel leakage may occur.
remedy: Replace the original hose clip with an alternative version designed to increase the clamping effect on the hose.

defect: There is a possibility that one or both of the brackets which attach the tailgate struts to the body 'C' pillars may bend allowing the strut to detach. This could permit the tailgate to close unexpectedly.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for reinforcement of both strut brackets and replacement of any brackets found to be bent.

defect: The engine wiring harness may chafe on the power steering pump pulley resulting in a possible fire hazard.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and secure the wiring harness with cable ties as per the manufacturers instructions. At the same time the wiring will be checked for damage and where this has occurred it will be rectified as required.

defect: The front latch hooks securing the convertible top to the windscreen frame may fracture and in the worst case allow the convertible top to retract without warning whilst the vehicle is being driven.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original latch hooks with modified versions.

defect: The starter motor terminal may fail causing interruption in the feed to various other electrical circuits. Such a failure would immobilise the vehicle and render the lighting system inoperative.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for modifications to the wiring which will prevent such an interruption from occurring.

defect: A specific batch of vehicles have been equipped with front suspension coil springs which may suffer from localised corrosion. This can cause breakage of the springs with an adverse effect on vehicle control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original coil springs with quality assured examples.

defect: On a specific batch of rear wheel bearings the outer bearing race may break up during certain operating conditions leading to failure of the bearing and hub detachment.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection and replacement of the affected bearings.

defect: The window operating switch may latch in the 'pressed' condition. This could result in the window continuing to operate up or down when pressure on the switch is released.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original window switches with quality assured units.

defect: The window operating switch may latch in the 'pressed' condition. This could result in the window continuing to operate up or down when pressure on the switch is released.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original window switches with quality assured units.

defect: Incorrect positioning and/or tightening of the fuel pipe clips on the injection bar may cause petrol fumes or smell in the passenger compartment.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection. Where the subject pipes have been incorrectly positioned and/or tightened the pipes will be replaced.

defect: 1) Certain cable looms in the engine compartment may chafe on adjacent sharp edges with the possibility of a short circuit. 2) Leakage may develop in the hose connections to the fuel manifold.
remedy: 1) Recall the affected vehicles re-route secure and protect the subject cable looms as required to eliminate chafing. 2) Replace the fuel hose securing clamps check the condition of the hoses and replace as required.

defect: The steel brake pipe from the master cylinder to the ABS valve block may chafe on the air cleaner hose. This could result in failure of the pipe with loss of braking on one circuit.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles shorten and re-route the air cleaner hose to avoid possible contact with the brake pipe. Where chafing has taken place the brake pipe will be replaced.

defect: A plastic clip may have been left in the engine air inlet hose during initial assembly. Should this clip be drawn into the throttle housing it may cause the throttle to jam.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the engine air inlet hose removing the clip (if present).

defect: Under certain conditions the alternator feed wire/terminal may contact the clutch cable and the instrument panel harness may chafe against the steering column. Either of these concerns could lead to short circuiting and.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles reposition the alternator terminal and secure the wiring harnesses in the bulkhead area away from moving parts.

defect: It is possible that the steering rack pinion nose bearing may have been omitted during manufacture. This would result in stiffness of the steering.
remedy: The affected vehicles will be recalled and examined to establish that the pinion nose bearing has been fitted. Where the bearing is found to be missing the steering rack will be replace with quality assured unit.

defect: The pawl spring fitted as original equipment to the parking brake may be insufficiently long and consequently fail to exert enough pressure to ensure that the pawl engages positively in the ratchet teeth. This could allow the parking brake to release
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original pawl spring with a longer version.

defect: The pawl spring fitted as original equipment to the parking brake may be insufficiently long and consequently fail to exert enough pressure to ensure that the pawl engages positively in the ratchet teeth. This could allow the parking brake to release
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original pawl spring with a longer version.

defect: Power steering fluid may leak from the top seal of the steering assembly pinion housing into the vehicle passenger compartment.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for fitment of a modified oil seal to the steering assembly pinion housing.

defect: The clamp bolt on one of three steering column universal couplings may not have been fully tightened on initial assembly. Should this bolt loosen it could allow excess free movement in the steering and if not rectified loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles check the torque of the subject bolt and where necessary re-tighten it to the manufacturers specifications. Where a clamp bolt is found to be below the specified torque the splines on the shaft will be examined for

defect: The clamp bolt on one of three steering column universal couplings may not have been fully tightened on initial assembly. Should this bolt loosen it could allow excess free movement in the steering and if not rectified loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles check the torque of the subject bolt and where necessary re-tighten it to the manufacturers specifications. Where a clamp bolt is found to be below the specified torque the splines on the shaft will be examined for

defect: The front suspension upper mounting plate cups may crack. Under certain conditions this could affect vehicle handling.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the front suspension upper mounting plates with examples incorporating an alternative metal specification.

defect: In a small batch of vehicles in the above chassis range very severe usage may produce deterioration of the chassis mounting points for the front suspension arms which could compromise the directional stability of the vehicle.
remedy: Recalled vehicles will be inspected and a reinforcement plate will be fitted accordingly.

defect: The injector retaining clamps may not have been correctly tightened. This could result in leakage of fuel from around the injectors.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and ensure that the injector clamp bolts are tightened to the manufacturers specification.

defect: A wiring harness routed behind the dashboard may chafe on the ECU mounting bracket. This could damage the loom and render several electrical circuits inoperative.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for the fitment of a protective covering on the ECU mounting bracket edge.

defect: A batch of vehicles has been identified where the parking brake pawl teeth have been incorrectly formed and are of insufficient depth. This may result in damage to the pawl teeth as well as those on the handbrake ratchet and could permit spontaneous release
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the parking brake ratchet and pawl mechanisms with quality assured components. This recall supersedes former campaign R1992/17 since Renault have decided to replace the ratchet and pawl mechanisms on

defect: A few instances of detachment of the brake pad friction material from the backing plate have occurred. This has only happened on Vauxhall Astras and Cavaliers equipped with these pads as replacement equipment and is restricted to a particular b
remedy: (Continued) Where this is the case the pads will be replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: A few instances of detachment of the brake pad friction material from the backing plate have occurred. This has only happened on Vauxhall Astras and Cavaliers equipped with these pads as replacement equipment and is restricted to a particular b
remedy: The distributors of the brake pads Eurotec Automotive Ltd have contacted all distributors and retailers asking them to return all unsold stock from the suspect batch. Additionally distributors and retailers have been requested to contact as far as po

defect: Due to the effects of age and temperature the underbonnet rubber fuel lines may harden. This could lead to the possibility of fuel leakage particularly when the engine is cold.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the existing fuel pipes with the modified versions introduced to production vehicles in 1992.

defect: The anti-lock brake electronic control unit may malfunction due to receiving a reversed polarity feed through its earthing system which shares a common earth point with other electrical systems on the vehicle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and alter the wiring system to provide a separate earthing point for the ABS system.

defect: A small number of subject vehicles may have been equipped with front brake discs of insufficient metal thickness. This could adversely affect braking performance.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for examination of the front brake discs. Where any disc does not meet the manufacturers dimensional specification both front discs will be renewed.

defect: On the subject vehicles it is possible that the brake pipe holder may not have been correctly positioned on the steering rack. This could allow the brake pipe to chafe on adjoining components and cause pipe damage.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and if necessary modify the position of the pipe holder and pipes to eliminate the possibility of the pipes chafing on other components.

defect: Air suspension driver's seat may inadvertently operate incorrectly positioning the driver in relation to the vehicle controls.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles to change the control system on the drivers seat.

defect: Cracking may occur in the steering drop arm or idler arm and bracket assembly which if not detected could ultimately affect steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for examination of the subject components. Any arms or brackets identified as belonging to the affected batches will be replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: Cracking may occur in the steering drop arm or idler arm and bracket assembly which if not detected could ultimately affect steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for examination of the subject components. Any arms or brackets identified as belonging to the affected batches will be replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: Cracking may occur in the steering drop arm or idler arm and bracket assembly which if not detected could ultimately affect steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for examination of the subject components. Any arms or brackets identified as belonging to the affected batches will be replaced with quality assured examples.

defect: A possible fault has been identified in the design of the recliner bar of this seat. This could affect the security of the occupant in sudden stop or accident applications.
remedy: Through contact with stockists and advertising in the Press recall all seats possibly affected by this concern. Where a seat with a faulty recliner bar is identified the seat unit will be replaced.

defect: Possible fracture of the stub axle(s) on high mileage passenger carrying vehicles. This could result in loss of the wheel and hub assembly with attendant loss of vehicle control and braking effort on one brake circuit.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the stub axle during normal routine servicing or repair with new units incorporating a revised heat treatment requirement.

defect: The weld attaching the stub axle to the suspension arm may fail resulting in collapse and displacement of the suspension
remedy: Recall the affected semi-trailers and replace the suspension arms with quality assured examples.

defect: Certain vehicles within the chassis range specified may have been fitted with examples of a batch of Dunlop tyres which are the subject of a recall. The tyres were affected by a contaminant during manufacture which could cause loss of adhesion between
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for examination of the tyres. Where any tyres from the affected batch are found they will be replaced.

defect: On some towbars manufactured within a specified period the welding between the ball unit brackets and the crossmember may be defective. In extreme cases this could result in trailer detachment.
remedy: Recall all 850 models which have been fitted with towbars and check if the towbar is within the affected range. Where it is established that this is the case the towbar assembly will be replaced with a quality assured unit.

defect: On a limited batch of caravan axles there exists a possibility of the expander clutch disengaging from the brake shoes. This is due to the introduction of a modified shoe which offers slightly less engagement with the expander clutch. Should the problem occur it may cause the brakes to bind or lock.
remedy: Recall the affected caravans for examination and rework as necessary. Where modified shoes are fitted the existing clutch will be replaced with a modified version. Additionally all boxes of replacement brake shoes will contain a warning that they must be fitted with the latest expander clutch.

defect: There is a possibility that a ball socket on the cruise control may detach. This could allow the linkage to jam on adjacent components and prevent the accelerator linkage returning to the idle position when the pedal is released.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original cruise control ball sockets with quality assured steel examples.

defect: Possible failure of the brake servo vacuum pump resulting in loss of service brake servo assistance.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for removal of the pump induced vacuum supply and conversion of the vacuum source to the engine induction system.

defect: The welds securing the front towing eye to its mounting bracket are not to specification and can result in detachment of the eye when the vehicle is under tow.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the welds which secure the front towing eye. Where these are not to specification the welds will be reworked as per the manufacturers instructions.

defect: The welds securing the front towing eye to its mounting bracket are not to specification and can result in detachment of the eye when the vehicle is under tow.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the welds which secure the front towing eye. Where these are not to specification the welds will be reworked as per the manufacturers instructions.

defect: Maintenance inspections have revealed cracking around the periphery of the weld retaining the king pin to the upper coupler apron plate on specified trailers.
remedy: Depending on the condition of the coupling on inspection it will either be reworked by the addition of stiffer plates or by the replacement of the welded-in king pin by a bolt-in king pin.

defect: Maintenance inspections have revealed cracking around the periphery of the weld retaining the king pin to the upper coupler apron plate on specified trailers.
remedy: Depending on the condition of the coupling on inspection it will either be reworked by the addition of stiffer plates or by the replacement of the welded-in king pin by a bolt-in king pin.

defect: Maintenance inspections have revealed cracking around the periphery of the weld retaining the king pin to the upper coupler apron plate on specified trailers.
remedy: Depending on the condition of the coupling on inspection it will either be reworked by the addition of stiffer plates or by the replacement of the welded-in king pin by a bolt-in king pin.

defect: The seam weld joining the wheel disc to the wheel rim may lack penetration resulting in failure of the weld and eventual detachment of the road wheel.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the road wheels with quality assured examples.

defect: The battery cable terminal may touch the starter motor solenoid body at the point of attachment to the starter motor. This could result in a short circuit.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the angle of attachment to the starter motor terminal. Where this is close to or touching the starter motor solenoid body it will be repositioned to ensure that adequate clearance is maintained.

defect: The battery cable terminal may touch the starter motor solenoid body at the point of attachment to the starter motor. This could result in a short circuit.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the angle of attachment to the starter motor terminal. Where this is close to or touching the starter motor solenoid body it will be repositioned to ensure that adequate clearance is maintained.

defect: The driveshaft retaining nuts may slacken due to defective peening.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the driveshaft retaining nuts for security. Any nut showing evidence of defective peening will be renewed and secured as per the manufacturers instructions.

defect: The driveshaft retaining nuts may slacken due to defective peening.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the driveshaft retaining nuts for security. Any nut showing evidence of defective peening will be renewed and secured as per the manufacturers instructions.

defect: The air tank mounting brackets may fracture resulting in insecurity of the air tanks.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for replacement of the original air tank mounting brackets with modified examples.

defect: It is possible that the battery cable may have been inadequately secured. This could allow the cable to chafe in the vicinity of an aperture in the secondary bulkhead and may result in a short circuit and in extreme cases damage to the battery cable.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to inspect and where necessary rework the battery cable.

defect: It is possible that the battery cable may have been inadequately secured. This could allow the cable to chafe in the vicinity of an aperture in the secondary bulkhead and may result in a short circuit and in extreme cases damage to the battery cable.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles to inspect and where necessary rework the battery cable.

defect: The single point injector cable harness may chafe against the cylinder head. This could result in short circuiting and burning of the harness.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the injector cable harness for indications of chafing making good where necessary before securing the harness to the throttle mechanism body.

defect: It is possible that the lateral tie rod joints may have been incorrectly fitted to the steering rack assembly. This could affect steering control of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for checking and where necessary replace the steering rack.

defect: The aluminium ferrules clamping the flexible fuel pipes on the pressure side of the injection system to their unions may deteriorate due to atmospheric conditions. In extreme cases this could allow fuel leakage with the possibility of an engine bay fire.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original flexible fuel pipes with modified versions.

defect: It is possible that certain brake pipes may not be secured to the vehicle underbody and may chafe on the front stabiliser bar. This could result in loss of brake fluid and reduced braking efficiency.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles. Re-route and secure the subject brake pipes using additional clips. Damaged brake pipes will be replaced where required

defect: It is possible that certain brake pipes may not be secured to the vehicle underbody and may chafe on the front stabiliser bar. This could result in loss of brake fluid and reduced braking efficiency.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles. Re-route and secure the subject brake pipes using additional clips. Damaged brake pipes will be replaced where required

defect: b) The light switch harness may chafe on the dash support with a consequent fire risk. Note that the scope of the defect will depend upon the particular chassis number of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and b) Secure the light switch harness and protect it by fitting beading to the edge of the dash support.

defect: a) The bolts/nuts securing respectively the steering rack and lower wishbone front unions may slacken. Loosening of either fastening could affect control of the vehicle. Note that the scope of the defect will depend upon the particular chassis number of the
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and a) Check the torque of the steering rack bolts and lower wishbone front union nuts tightening where necessary as per the instructions in the Volkswagen dealer bulletin.

defect: b) The light switch harness may chafe on the dash support with a consequent fire risk. Note that the scope of the defect will depend upon the particular chassis number of the vehicle.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and b) Secure the light switch harness and protect it by fitting beading to the edge of the dash support.

remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and a) Check the torque of the steering rack bolts and lower wishbone front union nuts tightening where necessary as per the instructions in the Volkswagen dealer bulletin.

defect: Due to manufacturing defect the handbrake can be inadvertently released from its applied position.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original handbrake assembly with a quality assured unit.

defect: One of several wiring looms located in the engine compartment may not be securely fixed. This could allow over a long time period the loom to chafe with the possibility of short circuiting and in extreme circumstances create a fire risk.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles. Fit protective sleeving to the loom in question and secure the assembly with clips.

defect: Oil may leak from the crimping on the power assisted steering high pressure hose. This could result in loss of steering power assistance.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and replace the original high pressure hose with a quality assured example.

defect: The mounting bracket for the dual horns may fracture and allow the horns to fall from the vehicle. As well as presenting a possible hazard to other traffic this could result in the steering being momentarily affected should the vehicle run over the
remedy: Recall affected vehicles and replace the original horn bracket with a stronger version.

defect: The vehicle may have been supplied with a different jack to that illustrated in the owner's handbook. This may cause the jack to be used in an incorrect manner.
remedy: To issue all owners/operators of affected vehicles with a supplement to the owner's handbook. This will incorporate additional diagrams and operating instructions to match the jack supplied with the vehicle.

defect: The bolts securing the steering arms to the stub axles may not have been sufficiently torqued at initial assembly. Should these bolts loosen this could lead to eventual loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and check the torque of the steering arm fixing bolts. Where this is found to be insufficient the bolts will be inspected and if necessary renewed.

defect: On vehicles equipped with ABS the sensor wires may be incorrectly connected. This could result in the sensing system failing to identify which wheel may be locking.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for inspection of the wiring connections and system function. Any instances of incorrect wiring will be corrected.

defect: Chafing may occur where two cables pass through a grommet in the front bulkhead. This could result in a short circuit and fire risk.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles. De-energise the 6 sq.mm. battery positive cable which backs up the engine management system by cutting it at both ends and taping it to the cable. An alternative arrangement is being made to back up the engine management system.

defect: The space frame body on these vehicles may be subject to cracking in the area of the rear suspension attachment.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles for reinforcement of the subject area of the frame.

defect: There is a possibility that the clutch lever may foul a moulded clip which secures the engine wiring harness. Should this occur the clip may open releasing the harness and making it liable to chafing and damage by the clutch lever.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and substitute a nylon fixing strap for the original moulded harness clip. This will ensure adequate operating clearance for the clutch lever.

defect: The bolts securing the front suspension struts to the wheel bearing housings may fracture due to brittleness. This could lead to loss of steering control.
remedy: Recall the affected vehicles and replace the original bolts with quality assured examples.

defect: A potential problem has been identified with the harness adjustment system on some Britax Freeway and Mothercare Rally child car seats. This could mean that the occupant is not afforded full protection in emergency stop or accident situations.
remedy: The manufacturer is advising purchasers of the problem via a press announcement and by notices at retailers. All affected seats will be replaced free of charge by the manufacturer on being contacted by the purchaser.

defect: The ignition lock cable harness may become damaged by chafing against the steering column. This could eventually cause a short circuit and possible fire risk.
remedy: Recall affected vehicles. Reposition the ignition lock cable harness and secure it clear of the steering column with a strip clip.

defect: The front seat pivoting mechanism may not operate correctly. This may lead to imprecise locking of the front seats which under certain driving conditions may have safety implications if the driving seat is not retained in the normal driving mo
remedy: Recall affected vehicles for replacement of the seat pivot flange and the fitment of an additional ring washer on both front seats.

defect: It is possible that due to pedal crank length there is insufficient clearance between the pedals and the front mudguard fixing. Under certain circumstances this could allow the rider's footwear to contact the fixing and interfere with steering control
remedy: Recall the affected cycles and replace the original 170mm pedal cranks with cranks of 150mm length to increase the clearance between the pedals and the mudguard fixing.
